questions.why: AI review comment with human approval under branch protection.

questions.q: You are identifying inefficiency in a Claude Code workflow where each engineer manually re-explains the project’s conventions and architecture in every session. Which adjustment most directly removes this inefficiency?
options: Capture the project’s conventions and architecture in a project-scoped CLAUDE.md (or equivalent persistent project-context file) committed to the repository, so each session loads it automatically.
Forbid the use of Claude Code on the project entirely to avoid the session-initialization overhead, accepting that the team loses all AI-assisted development productivity for this codebase.
Tell each engineer to retype the project conventions and architecture context more quickly at the start of each session, reducing time lost without eliminating the repeated manual effort.
Remove all documented project conventions and architectural standards so engineers have nothing to re-explain at session start, accepting the loss of consistency and shared coding standards.
questions.why: Project CLAUDE.md committed to the repo loads automatically each session.

questions.q: The compliance team has authored a regulatory disclosure procedure that must be applied identically across customer service, sales, and onboarding workflows. The procedure changes when regulators issue updates, currently four to six times per year. You are designing how the procedure will be packaged for use by Claude across all three workflows. Which two design decisions should you include? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: Reference the same Claude Skill from all three of the workflow integrations directly.
Store the procedure in a shared retrieval corpus accessed by all three workflows.
Have each workflow team rewrite the procedure for that team’s specific context.
Package the procedure as a Claude Skill owned by the compliance team directly.
Embed the procedure text into each workflow’s system prompt at integration time.
questions.why: One compliance-owned Skill referenced by all workflows gives single-source updates.

questions.q: You are resolving a Claude Code operational issue reported by the team and must complete the diagnostic steps before applying a targeted fix. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE applying the targeted fix? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: Open a permanent change request in the change-management system to formalize the upcoming fix.
Document the root cause and the fix in the team runbook for future occurrences.
Form a hypothesis about the most likely root cause given the symptom, configuration, and recent changes.
Reproduce the issue with a minimal reproduction case to confirm the symptom and isolate variables.
Notify the affected users that a fix has been deployed and the operational issue is resolved.
questions.why: Diagnosis precedes the fix: reproduce minimally and form a root-cause hypothesis.

questions.q: A Claude architect is configuring a shared Claude Code environment for a twelve-person development team. Which two configuration decisions most directly establish a consistent, secure team environment? (Choose two.)
options: applying managed configuration to enforce non-overridable security and compliance policies across all team members
committing shared MCP server definitions and tool permissions in project-scope configuration files alongside the repository
instructing each engineer to configure their preferred Claude model in personal user-scope settings
storing the team’s shared API key in the project-scope settings.json so all engineers use the same credential
setting editor theme and display preferences at the project scope so they are uniform across workstations
questions.why: Managed settings are non-overridable policy and project-scope .mcp.json/settings.json are committed for team sharing.

questions.q: You are configuring Claude Code for a team that needs every engineer to share the same MCP server set, permission rules, and project context across the engineering monorepo. Which configuration scope best supports this requirement?
options: user scope configured individually on each engineer’s machine, with no shared configuration committed to the repository and no guarantee of consistency across the team
user scope with the MCP server definitions and permission rules placed in each engineer’s ~/.claude/settings.json and synchronized manually via a shared setup script outside version control
local scope configured only on the lead architect’s machine, with no configuration present on other engineers’ machines and no mechanism to distribute MCP servers or permission rules
project scope, with the configuration committed to the repository so every engineer working in the project picks up the same MCP servers, permissions, and context
questions.why: Project scope committed to the repo shares MCP servers, permissions and context.

questions.q: A Claude needs to ensure that a security-hardening flag cannot be disabled by any individual engineer after it is set. Which configuration scope correctly enforces this requirement?
options: managed configuration applied centrally and marked as non-overridable
environment variable defined in the CI/CD pipeline only
project scope (.claude/settings.json) committed to the repository
user scope (~/.claude/settings.json) on each engineer’s machine
questions.why: Managed settings have the highest precedence and cannot be overridden by user, project or local settings.

questions.q: You are integrating Claude Code into a workflow that runs against a production database. Which guardrail design most directly preserves safety on data-modifying operations?
options: Allow Claude Code to write directly to the production database without subagent scoping, read-only credential defaults, or human confirmation gates on data-modifying operations.
Configure the database MCP server with a fully privileged credential that can perform any read or write operation, and allow all operations to proceed without explicit human confirmation.

Configure the database MCP server with a read-only credential by default, restrict the subagent’s tool list to read-only operations, and require explicit human confirmation on any operation that would modify data.
Disable all logging and auditing on database operations through the MCP server to reduce alert noise, removing the observability needed to detect unintended data modifications.
questions.why: Read-only credentials, read-only subagent tools and human confirmation on writes is layered least privilege.

questions.q: A Claude architect is auditing configuration scope assignments. Which two statements correctly identify an appropriate use of user-scope configuration versus other scopes? (Choose two.)
options: defining MCP server endpoints shared by all contributors to a specific repository
persisting personal editor theme preferences that follow an engineer across projects
saving a preferred Claude response language that applies to all repositories the engineer uses
storing API authentication keys so they are not committed to version control
enforcing a company-wide policy that disables a feature for all engineers
questions.why: User scope holds personal preferences that follow an engineer across projects.
questions.note: Ambiguous item. Also defensible: "storing API authentication keys so they are not committed to version control".

questions.q: You are rolling out a standardized Claude Code configuration to an engineering team and must complete the planning steps before piloting the configuration. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE piloting the configuration with a small group of engineers? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: Roll out the stabilized configuration to additional teams with documentation and a defined support channel.
Define the project-scope baseline covering Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, permission rules, and subagents.
Onboard every engineer in the organization to the new configuration through mandatory training sessions.
Iterate the configuration based on the pilot findings and stabilize the baseline before broader rollout.
Identify the team workflows, security boundaries, and which decisions belong to managed configuration versus project scope.
questions.why: Planning steps before piloting are defining the project-scope baseline and identifying workflows and managed-versus-project boundaries.

questions.q: You are supporting a team whose Claude Code sessions consistently load 60 or more MCP tools from many servers, exhausting context budget before the session begins. Which adjustment most directly addresses this issue without removing capability?
options: Enable Tool Search so tool definitions are deferred and discovered on demand rather than loaded into context upfront.
Add additional MCP servers to give the team more capability, which increases rather than reduces the number of tool definitions loaded into the session’s context budget.
Increase the prompt’s verbosity with additional instructions and context, which consumes more of the context budget rather than reducing the tool-definition overhead causing the issue.
Disable every MCP server in the configuration to free up context budget, accepting that the team loses all tool access and cannot perform any MCP-dependent task in the session.
questions.why: Tool Search defers MCP tool definitions and loads them on demand.
questions.note: Current Claude Code documentation describes tool search as on by default, so this scenario reflects an older default.

questions.q: A team manager wants all engineers working on the same repository to share identical MCP server definitions without manual synchronization. Which configuration approach satisfies this requirement?
options: project-scope .claude/settings.json and .mcp.json files committed to the repository
managed configuration pushed to all endpoints by the administrator
environment variables set at the operating-system level on each workstation
each engineer maintains a personal ~/.claude/settings.json with the shared definitions
questions.why: Committing .mcp.json (project scope) shares MCP server definitions via version control.

questions.q: You are explaining the precedence of Claude Code configuration scopes to the team. Which precedence ordering, from highest to lowest, is correct?
options: Local --> managed --> user --> command-line arguments --> project
Managed --> command-line arguments --> local --> project --> user
User --> project --> local --> command-line arguments --> managed
Project --> user --> managed --> local --> project command-line arguments
questions.why: Managed > command line > local > project > user.

questions.q: You are reviewing a peer’s Claude Code permission rules for an enterprise rollout. The rules grant unrestricted Bash access to all projects across all developers. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Approve the unrestricted Bash access as written on the grounds that narrowing the rules would add configuration complexity, accepting the full attack surface for all engineers across all projects.
Replace unrestricted Bash with narrowly-scoped tool patterns that allow only the specific commands the workflows require, and add explicit deny rules for sensitive operations.
Add unrestricted access to additional tool categories as well, so that Bash is not asymmetrically more permissive than other tools, expanding the attack surface further in the name of consistency.
Disable all permission rules for the enterprise rollout so every command across every project runs without any tool-pattern scoping or explicit deny rules for sensitive operations.
questions.why: Least privilege means narrowly scoped allow patterns plus explicit deny rules.

questions.q: You are integrating AI-assisted tooling into the teams documentation workflow. The team wants generated documentation that stays grounded in the actual code. Which integration approach best fits this requirement?
options: Disable all filesystem and code-search tools so the subagents cannot read any repository code, accepting that documentation generation will be entirely disconnected from the actual implementation.
Generate documentation from the model’s training-data recall without reading any of the actual repository code, accepting that the output will not reflect the current implementation.
Configure subagents that read the relevant code files via filesystem and code-search tools, generate the documentation, and emit changes through the teams normal review workflow.
Have the subagents publish generated documentation directly to the public-facing site without passing through the team’s normal review workflow or any human approval step.
questions.why: Grounded docs need code reading and normal review workflow.

questions.q: You are supporting an engineer whose newly added MCP server does not appear in their Claude Code session. Which diagnostic step should be tried first?
options: Reinstall the developer’s operating system from scratch, discarding all local configuration and tool state before attempting any targeted diagnostic steps.
Disable every MCP server in the configuration to isolate the issue, removing all tool access rather than confirming whether the new server is registered.
Switch the team to a different Claude product family unrelated to the existing workflow, abandoning the current configuration rather than diagnosing the registration issue.
Verify the MCP server is registered using the listing command, then reconnect the session if needed, since configuration changes typically require a restart to take effect.
questions.why: Check registration with claude mcp list or /mcp and reconnect or restart as needed.

questions.q: You are identifying the highest-impact optimization for a deployment whose token cost is dominated by a long, repeated system prompt and a large retrieved context per request. Which optimization most directly targets the dominant cost driver?
options: Batch requests so that several queries share a single call and the system prompt is transmitted once for the whole group.
Move the long, repeated system prompt into a cacheable prefix and trim retrieved context to the spans relevant to each query.
Compress the system prompt by rewriting its instructions more concisely and removing examples that overlap with one another.
Route simpler requests to a smaller model and reserve the larger model for cases that a lightweight classifier flags as complex.
questions.why: Prompt caching of the repeated prefix plus trimming retrieved context targets the dominant cost.

questions.q: You are configuring tool permissions for a Claude-based assistant. The assistant’s defined responsibilities require read access to a knowledge base and write access to a draft queue, and nothing else. Which scoping design best applies least privilege?
options: Allow-list every read tool in the catalog globally, and scope only the write-draft-queue tool to the assistant’s specific role.
Per-role allow-list of exactly the read-knowledge-base and write-draft-queue tools, enforced at the orchestration layer.
Scope the assistant to the knowledge-base and draft-queue tools, granting both read and write on each for operational flexibility.
Allow access to all tools with read permissions globally, restricting only write permissions to the draft-queue tool.
questions.why: Exact per-role allow-list enforced at orchestration is least privilege.

questions.q: You are preparing an operational runbook for a Claude-based service. Which content is essential to include in the runbook?
options: a post-incident review template, a historical incident log, blameless retrospective guidelines, and a tracker for follow-up action items
a general on-call rotation schedule, a team contact list, shift handoff notes, and paging preferences for each responder
a glossary of system architecture terms, a service dependency map, a component ownership table, and diagrams of data flow between services
common alerts and their triage steps, escalation paths, rollback procedures, and references to the relevant dashboards and logs
questions.why: Runbooks need alerts triage, escalation, rollback and dashboard references.

questions.q: You are assessing a Claude-based system whose dominant risk is silent quality drift on safety-relevant outputs after a model-version upgrade. Which assessment activity most directly addresses this risk?
options: Refresh the adversarial evaluation set before each upgrade with newly written inputs so the scoring reflects current threat patterns.
Instrument the production path to capture user reports and flagged outputs so safety regressions are detected after each upgrade.
Maintain an adversarial evaluation set with version-attributed scoring so each upgrade is measured against the same set before promotion.
Expand the adversarial evaluation set after each upgrade with cases drawn from the newest version’s observed failure modes.
questions.why: A stable set with version-attributed scoring enables like-for-like comparison across upgrades.

questions.q: You are reviewing a customer-support agent’s configuration. Each candidate tool falls into one of four categories: (1) required to complete defined tasks, (2) frequently used and reduces hand-offs, (3) occasionally useful for unrelated work, (4) speculative future utility. Which categories should typically remain in the agent configuration?
options: Category 1 only, because least privilege means the minimal set that completes defined tasks.
Categories 1, 2, and 3, because retaining occasionally useful tools avoids reconfiguring the agent when new requests arrive.
Categories 1 and 2 only, because they map to defined tasks and the agent’s regular hand-offs.
All 4 categories, because broader tool access tends to help agent performance, whether or not a tool maps to a defined task.
questions.why: Least privilege keeps tools mapped to defined tasks and regular hand-offs.
questions.note: Ambiguous item. Also defensible: "Category 1 only, because least privilege means the minimal set that completes defined tasks".

questions.q: You are designing a content moderation classifier that processes high volumes of user-generated comments under a tight per-message latency budget using well-defined classification labels. Which model selection best aligns with the workload?
options: Haiku
Fable
Opus
Sonnet
questions.why: Haiku is the fastest tier for high-volume, latency-sensitive classification.

questions.q: You are identifying signals that a deployment should re-enter design rather than continue iterating in place. Which signal most directly indicates the need for a new design cycle?
options: Several runbook steps have drifted out of date and describe procedures that no longer match how the service operates.
Multiple customer-facing strings use inconsistent terminology, and support tickets show users are confused by the mismatched wording.
A dashboard alert fires constantly because its threshold was set before recent traffic growth changed the normal baseline volume.
The systems current architecture cannot meet the new requirements without changes to component responsibilities or core contracts.
questions.why: Needing changes to component responsibilities or core contracts requires a new design cycle.

questions.q: You are transitioning a Claude-based deployment from design into implementation. Which handoff package most directly supports a clean transition?
options: architecture overview, ADRs, component contracts, evaluation framework with reference set, runbooks, on-call playbook, and known limitations
an architecture overview and component contracts, with the evaluation framework and on-call playbook left for the implementation team to create after handoff
an architecture overview delivered verbally in a kickoff meeting, with no written component contracts, evaluation framework, or runbooks to accompany it
a project charter and stakeholder sign-off record, treated as sufficient governance to proceed with implementation
questions.why: Most complete written handoff package.

questions.q: You are designing the prompt for a ticket-triage classifier with thirty well-defined categories and clear category descriptions in the prompt. Which technique is most appropriate as the starting point?
options: a prompt-chaining setup that routes each ticket through a coarse grouping step before selecting the final category
a chain-of-thought prompt for a routing decision that does not require multi-step reasoning
a zero-shot prompt that specifies the categories with their descriptions and the required output format
a prompt with no category descriptions, expecting the model to infer the category set
questions.why: Zero-shot with clear category descriptions and output format is the right starting point.

questions.q: A security team is evaluating two proposed controls. Control A adds an outbound tool allow-list with destination restrictions and per-call review. Control B scores responses against a stable adversarial evaluation set after each model-version change. Which two risk categories are correctly matched to these controls? (Choose two.)
options: Control B -> undetected behavioral regression following a model change
Control B -> unauthorized data leaving the system through tool invocations
Control A -> unauthorized data leaving the system through tool invocations
Control A -> prompt injection from adversarial content in retrieved data
Control A -> undetected behavioral regression following a model change
questions.why: Allow-list controls tool-based exfiltration; stable adversarial set detects regression after model change.

questions.q: You are a platform architect designing an internal Claude-based assistant that serves both finance analysts and external auditors. Each population must access only documents permitted by their role. Where should role-based access control be enforced in the pipeline?
options: at the retrieval layer, before any role-restricted content reaches the prompt construction step or the model
inside the system prompt as a natural-language instruction that names the specific role-based access groups Claude should treat as unauthorized
at the retrieval layer, but relying on a single organization-wide access token shared across all roles rather than per-role scoping
after the response is generated, by post-filtering content that should not have been retrieved
questions.why: Access control must be enforced before restricted content reaches the model.

questions.q: You are reviewing a peer’s draft system prompt that contains contradictory instructions: one section says to never speculate beyond the supplied source, and another says to confidently fill in any gaps. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Add a priority-ordering instruction that tells the model to evaluate all available instructions and apply the most contextually appropriate one on each request.
Keep both contradictory instructions in place and add a third instruction telling the model to use its best judgment based on the query’s context.
Keep both contradictory instructions in place and rely on the model to select which one to follow on each individual request, accepting inconsistent behavior as a result.
Resolve the contradiction by removing or rewording the gap-filling instruction so the prompt consistently constrains the model to source-supported content.
questions.why: Contradictory instructions should be resolved by editing the prompt, not delegated to the model.

questions.q: You are integrating human review into a high-volume classification pipeline where reviewing every output is not possible. Which sampling strategy best balances throughput with quality oversight?
options: risk-stratified sampling that reviews all low-confidence and high-impact outputs and a smaller random sample of high-confidence routine outputs
inverse sampling that reviews only high-confidence routine outputs and skips all low-confidence and high-impact outputs
universal sampling that reviews every output without regard to confidence level or throughput impact
no sampling at all, relying on user-submitted complaints to surface quality and safety issues
questions.why: Risk-stratified sampling balances throughput and oversight.

questions.q: You are comparing two configurations for an internal compliance Q&A assistant. Configuration X reduces top-k retrieval and serves with a lighter model, lowering p95 latency by 38 percent at a measured 2 percent drop on the accuracy benchmark. Configuration Y keeps top-k and the heavier model, with p95 latency unchanged and no measurable accuracy change. The deployment’s stated priorities are accuracy first and latency second. Which configuration is the better recommendation?
options: Configuration X, because a 38 percent latency improvement outweighs a 2 percent accuracy reduction as a general rule across compliance deployments.
Configuration X, because the 2 percent accuracy reduction falls within normal benchmark variance and is not a meaningful regression here.
Configuration X, because lower latency generally matters more than accuracy, independent of this deployment’s stated priorities.
Configuration Y, because the deployment’s stated priority is accuracy first, and Configuration X reduces measured accuracy.
questions.why: Stated priority is accuracy first, and X measurably reduces accuracy.

questions.q: You are a solution architect designing a Claude-based assistant with access to 60 internal tools across multiple business domains. Loading every tool definition on every request increases token usage and time to first response. Which design pattern best addresses this issue without sacrificing capability breadth?
options: Increase the maximum context length so all 60 tool definitions fit within a single request without exceeding the limit.
Group the 60 tools into five fixed categories and load one category per request based on a static mapping of task type to category.
Use a separate model call to condense all 60 tool definitions into a compact index that is prepended to each user turn for tool selection.
Apply progressive tool discovery so a curated initial subset is exposed and additional tools are loaded on demand based on the task.
questions.why: Tool search with defer_loading loads a small initial set and discovers other tools on demand.

questions.q: You are supporting an engineer whose Claude Code session reports a permission denial when the engineer expected the action to be allowed. Which resolution step is most appropriate?
options: Add a broad allow-list entry at the user scope so the action is permitted in this session and in all future sessions.
Inspect the active permission rules across all scopes to identify which rule is denying the action and confirm whether it should be amended.
Amend the permission rules at the local scope to allow the action, then re-run it to confirm the denial no longer occurs.
Run the action outside Claude Code and paste the output back into the session so the engineer can continue without interruption.
questions.why: Inspect which rule in which scope denies the action before amending anything.

questions.q: You are diagnosing a Claude Code session whose subagent uses 50,000 tokens of context before the engineer types a single message. Which root cause is most likely?
options: A retrieved-context preload step runs automatically at session start, pulling in reference documents that occupy context budget before the engineer types anything.
A verbose system prompt with extensive background instructions is loaded at session start, consuming a large share of the context budget before the first message.
A large project-scoped CLAUDE.md file is loaded automatically at session start, contributing substantial content to the context budget before any message is typed.
Many MCP servers are configured, each contributing tool definitions to the context budget; Tool Search is not enabled, so all definitions load upfront.
questions.why: Many MCP tool definitions loaded upfront are the likeliest large pre-message cost in a subagent, though a large CLAUDE.md is plausible.
questions.note: Ambiguous item. Also defensible: "A large project-scoped CLAUDE.md file is loaded automatically at session start, contributing substantial content to the context budget before any message is typed". Current Claude Code documentation describes tool search as on by default, so this scenario reflects an older default.

questions.q: You are operating an interactive assistant whose dominant performance constraint is per-turn latency. Quality on routine turns is already acceptable. Which configuration adjustment most directly improves latency without disproportionately damaging quality?
options: Cache the full corpus in memory ahead of each request.
Switch to a smaller model for every turn in place of prompt caching.
Reduce retrieval depth to the top-k passages that historically cover the answer, and cache stable system-prompt content.
Precompute and cache retrieval embeddings offline, keeping retrieval depth and model tier unchanged.
questions.why: Smaller retrieval depth plus prompt caching cuts latency without a model downgrade.

questions.q: You are defining escalation criteria for ambiguous cases in an automated workflow. Which set of criteria best supports consistent escalation?
options: case age and the requester’s department, applied inconsistently across teams with no confidence threshold or classifier-based ambiguity flag
prior customer complaints and the requesting user’s seniority level, with no confidence threshold or content-classifier ambiguity flag
confidence threshold below a defined level, presence of high-impact decision categories, ambiguity flags raised by content classifiers, and the user’s explicit request for review
a confidence threshold below a defined level and the on-call engineer’s personal preference, with no defined impact category or ambiguity-flag criterion
questions.why: Confidence, impact, ambiguity flags and explicit request give consistent escalation.

questions.q: You are running a controlled experiment to compare two prompts and must complete the design steps before executing the experiment. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE running the experiment with random assignment? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: Document the recommendation, the trade-offs accepted, and the alternatives considered.
Monitor interim metrics daily during the experiment and stop as soon as one prompt appears ahead.
Define the hypothesis and the primary success metric for the comparison.
Decide whether to promote, reject, or iterate the candidate based on the analysis.
Determine the minimum detectable effect size and the sample size needed for power.
questions.why: Hypothesis/primary metric and MDE/sample size precede the run.

questions.q: You are compiling factors that should drive the choice between Model Context Protocol (MCP). direct API integration, and agent-to-agent handoff. Which two factors belong on the list? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
options: whether the integration must be portable across multiple AI clients in the ecosystem
whether the organization has a documented naming convention for internal API endpoints
whether the interaction is stateless and latency-sensitive or stateful and longer-running
whether the underlying transport supports encryption in transit between the integrated services
whether the team has prior implementation experience with any of the candidate protocols
questions.why: Portability across clients and stateless vs stateful interaction drive the pattern choice.

questions.q: A pilot AI assistant for procurement specialists shows 89 percent first-response acceptance, but follow-up surveys reveal that specialists frequently override the assistant’s vendor recommendations after consulting unrelated criteria the assistant did not consider. The pilot owner wants to ship the assistant as is, given the strong acceptance rate. Which two discernment-competency observations should you raise BEFORE approving the launch? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: The pilot duration was likely too short to establish reliability across the full year.
The unconsidered criteria represent a scope gap in the assistant’s input space directly.
Acceptance does not measure whether recommendations are right after specialist review.
The survey response rate may not be statistically representative of all the specialists.
The acceptance rate, combined with the pilot’s sample size, is enough evidence to proceed without further review.
questions.why: Overrides reveal a scope gap and acceptance rate does not measure correctness after specialist review.

questions.q: A research summarization assistant has been deployed for six months. A user has flagged that a generated summary contained a fabricated citation. The product team has asked whether the incident requires architectural action or whether it is an isolated case. Which two Diligence-competency actions should you take? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: Sample recent summaries to estimate the fabrication frequency across the population.
Lower the model’s sampling temperature across the pipeline in response to the incident.
Review whether citation grounding controls exist anywhere in the current generation pipeline.
Communicate to users that the assistant does not fabricate output as a matter of design.
Disable the assistant immediately for all current users without any prior diagnostic analysis.
questions.why: Diligence means measuring prevalence and checking whether grounding controls exist.
